original_statement:
What did you do? List the exact steps to reproduce, in order. Run aspergillus's check-duplicates against a codebase containing near-miss or semantic duplicates (type-3/type-4 clones): two functions that share a substantial copied spine — a verbatim-identical inner closure plus an identical call, and duplicated statement sequences — embedded in two structurally different functions. (Originally observed in exophial3 on src/e_new_model/shell/drive.py:drive vs src/e_new_model/shell/driver.py:put.)
What did you expect to happen? check-duplicates flags (a) type-3 near-miss/gapped clones (copied fragments inside differently-shaped functions with added/removed/changed statements) and (b) type-4 semantic clones (functionally equivalent, syntactically different code) — or at minimum states in its own docs that its scope is type-2-only.
What actually happened? Include the exact error text or output. The detector at python/src/aspergillus/duplicates.py normalizes each function body (identifiers -> _ID, literals -> type markers; _Normalizer), renders the whole normalized body, sha256-hashes it (_hash_function), and groups only functions whose ENTIRE normalized body hashes identically (find_duplicate_groups). Fragment-level near-miss (type-3) and semantically-equivalent-but-syntactically-different (type-4) matches never produce a hit, on any input, by construction of the whole-body-hash comparison; a substantial duplicated spine embedded in two differently-shaped functions yields 'no duplicate functions found'. duplicates.py's own docstring self-declares 'This is what makes the hash a type-2 clone signature'.
Which surface or component? (e.g. gateway route, mobile screen, CLI verb) aspergillus check-duplicates (python/src/aspergillus/duplicates.py: _Normalizer, _hash_function, find_duplicate_groups)
What environment and version? (OS, app/gateway build or commit, network) aspergillus repo, Python rule pack (python/)
Is it reproducible? (always / intermittently / once) — and how often. always
What is the impact / severity? Who is blocked and how badly? The duplication gate is scoped to type-2 (renamed whole-function) clones only. Type-3 near-miss/gapped clones and type-4 semantic clones pass the gate uncaught. Standard type-1..4 clone taxonomy (Roy & Cordy clone-detection survey; Bellon et al. clone-tool comparison).
What activity was underway when this was found? (ODC Activity — e.g. testing, code review, normal usage, reproduction attempt) design review
What condition or event exposed the defect? (ODC Trigger — e.g. a config change, concurrent access, a boundary/edge-case input, an unusual workload) design conformance
Which quality/capability dimension does this affect? (ODC Impact — e.g. reliability, usability, capability, performance, security, maintainability, standards, requirements — distinct from the severity/who's-blocked question above) maintainability

Decomposed child: Replace aspergillus's current type-2 clone detector in python/src/aspergillus/duplicates.py — which normalizes identifiers to _ID and literals to type markers via _Normalizer, sha256-hashes the ENTIRE normalized function body via _hash_function, and groups only functions whose entire normalized body hashes identically via find_duplicate_groups — with a fragment-granular comparison. Keep the _Normalizer identifier->_ID / literal->type-marker normalization, but compare over SLIDING WINDOWS of normalized statement sequences instead of one whole-body hash, so a copied spine embedded inside a larger, differently-shaped function is caught. This fixes the defect where a copied spine — a verbatim-identical inner closure plus an identical call, plus duplicated statement sequences — embedded in two structurally different functions is missed today because the comparison hashes the entire normalized body (duplicates.py's own docstring self-declares the hash is 'a type-2 clone signature' over the whole body). Each detected type-2 pair must carry its clone type label and a similarity score, and boilerplate (trivial dunders/getters/pass-only bodies) must be excluded. Build a pytest suite including: fixtures from the Roy & Cordy (2007) editing-scenario taxonomy for type-2 edits, Bellon et al. (2007) reference clones, BigCloneBench (Svajlenko et al. 2014) pairs labeled T2, and the regression fixture from the original report — two functions (originally observed in exophial3 as src/e_new_model/shell/drive.py:drive vs src/e_new_model/shell/driver.py:put) sharing a verbatim copied spine embedded in two structurally different bodies, which currently yields 'no duplicate functions found' and must now be flagged.
restatement: The duplicate-function detector in python/src/aspergillus/duplicates.py hashes the whole normalized function body. Its function find_duplicate_groups groups two functions only when their whole-body hashes match exactly. This method misses a real defect class. A copied spine — an identical inner closure, an identical call, and a duplicated statement sequence — can sit inside two functions that differ elsewhere. The whole-body hashes then differ, so the tool reports no duplicate. The reported case is exophial3's function drive in src/e_new_model/shell/drive.py against exophial3's function put in src/e_new_model/shell/driver.py. These two functions share a verbatim copied spine inside two structurally different bodies. Today check-duplicates reports 'no duplicate functions found' for this pair. The fix keeps the _Normalizer's identifier-to-_ID and literal-to-type-marker normalization unchanged. The fix replaces the single whole-body hash with a sliding-window comparison over sequences of normalized statements. This sliding-window comparison catches a copied spine wherever it sits inside a function, not only when the spine is the whole function. Each reported type-2 clone pair must carry a clone-type label and a numeric similarity score. The detector must never report a boilerplate body as a duplicate. Boilerplate bodies are trivial dunder methods, simple getters, and pass-only bodies. This exclusion applies even when two boilerplate bodies match verbatim. The change ships with a pytest suite. The suite proves the general fragment-detection capability. The suite reproduces the drive/put regression. The suite proves boilerplate exclusion. The suite adds three further fixtures, each labeled for one clone-detection research source: the Roy & Cordy (2007) type-2 editing-scenario taxonomy, the Bellon et al. (2007) reference-clone benchmark, and the BigCloneBench corpus from Svajlenko et al. (2014). The detector must flag each of these three fixtures as a type-2 duplicate.

restatement_clauses.text: The detector replaces the whole-body hash comparison with a sliding-window comparison over normalized statement sequences. This change lets it catch a copied spine embedded inside a larger, differently-shaped function.
The _Normalizer's identifier-to-_ID and literal-to-type-marker normalization stays exactly as it is today.
Every reported type-2 clone pair carries a clone-type label.
Every reported type-2 clone pair carries a numeric similarity score.
The detector excludes boilerplate bodies — trivial dunder methods, simple getters, and pass-only bodies — from duplicate reporting, even when two such bodies match verbatim.

The regression fixture — function drive from exophial3's src/e_new_model/shell/drive.py and function put from exophial3's src/e_new_model/shell/driver.py, sharing a verbatim copied spine inside two structurally different bodies — is now flagged as a duplicate pair, where it previously produced 'no duplicate functions found'.
The pytest suite includes a fixture labeled for the Roy & Cordy (2007) type-2 editing-scenario taxonomy, and the detector flags it as a duplicate.
The pytest suite includes a fixture labeled for the Bellon et al. (2007) reference-clone benchmark, and the detector flags it as a duplicate.
The pytest suite includes a fixture labeled for the BigCloneBench (Svajlenko et al. 2014) type-2 (T2) clone category, and the detector flags it as a duplicate.

goal: Make aspergillus's duplicate detector catch a copied statement spine embedded inside two differently-shaped functions, label and score every reported pair, exclude boilerplate, and prove all of this with a pytest suite covering the drive/put regression and three named clone-research fixtures.
acceptance_criteria: A person runs the duplicate checker on two functions with different surrounding code but the same inner helper and the same duplicated block. The checker reports the two functions as a duplicate pair.
A person runs the normalizer on two functions that differ only in variable names and literal values. The normalizer still marks them as identical, exactly as it does today.
A person runs the duplicate checker on a known pair of duplicate functions. The reported pair carries a clone-type label.
A person runs the duplicate checker on a known pair of duplicate functions. The reported pair carries a similarity score above zero.
A person runs the duplicate checker on two files that share the same trivial pass-only __init__ method and the same one-line getter. The checker does not report them as duplicates.
A person runs the duplicate checker on the drive/put regression fixture. The checker reports drive and put as a duplicate pair, instead of the old 'no duplicate functions found' result.
A person runs the duplicate checker on the Roy & Cordy type-2 editing-scenario fixture. The checker reports its two functions as a duplicate pair.
A person runs the duplicate checker on the Bellon et al. reference-clone fixture. The checker reports its two functions as a duplicate pair.
A person runs the duplicate checker on the BigCloneBench T2 fixture. The checker reports its two functions as a duplicate pair.
